Lumen Code

Turn files into
moving light

The sender plays your file as an animated colour code; the receiver scans it with a camera and rebuilds it. No network, Bluetooth or pairing — everything stays in the browser.

Send

Pick a file and the screen plays the code. Density adapts to the screen, phone or desktop.

Start →

Receive

Point your camera at the sender’s screen. Save the file once enough data arrives.

Start →

Photosensitivity warning: while sending, the code flashes up to 60 times a second. If flashing light affects you (e.g. photosensitive epilepsy), don’t look at it.

Adaptive density

Cell size follows the physical screen size, so even small phone screens scan reliably.

Fountain coded

Every frame carries new data. Dropped or out-of-order frames don’t matter.

Colour + error correction

2–3 bits per cell, Reed–Solomon, per-packet checksums.

Zero dependencies, two engines

JavaScript and Rust/WASM implementations with bit-identical frames; no libraries, nothing leaves the device.

An open protocol

Lumen Code 1.0 has a complete specification (English and Chinese) and two reference implementations, JavaScript and Rust, that pass the same conformance test vectors. There is no package to install: point your coding agent at the repository and it can add Lumen Code to your app.

Specification Developer guides Test vectors Source on GitHub

Native apps

Desktop (macOS, Windows, Linux): download from GitHub Releases. iOS and Android: build from source. The apps use 120 Hz screens, high-frame-rate cameras and manual exposure, so they are usually faster than the web pages.

Download for desktop Build from source

Files go from screen to camera only, never through a server. Note: the receiver needs HTTPS or localhost to access the camera.
